request.spec:
A bulk settle is now all-or-nothing: if any selected claim cannot be settled by the signed-in
user (any refusal the single settle would give; going to PENDING is not a refusal), none of them is
settled, every one counts as refused and nothing is written. Otherwise every selected claim is
settled in list order as before, and after the claims' own lines one line BATCH_SETTLED
batch=<batch number> count=<claims in the batch> total=<the frozen figures of those SETTLED, added
up> is written.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A bulk settle is now all-or-nothing: if any selected claim cannot be settled by the signed-in
user (any refusal the single settle would give; going to PENDING is not a refusal), none of them is
settled, every one counts as refused and nothing is written. Otherwise every selected claim is
settled in list order as before, and after the claims' own lines one line BATCH_SETTLED
batch=<batch number> count=<claims in the batch> total=<the frozen figures of those SETTLED, added
up> is written.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Bulk settle is now all-or-nothing, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What it does now:**
- **First pass, nothing written:** every selected claim goes through all the checks a single settle makes. If any of them would be refused, or the selection includes a claim that doesn't exist, nothing is settled. The result is `settled 0, refused <all selected>`, nothing goes to the store or audit file, and no batch number is used up.
- **Otherwise:** each claim is settled in list order, exactly as before (one a clerk sends to PENDING still counts as settled and joins the batch). The claims get the sheet's next batch number. After their own lines, one more line is written: `BATCH_SETTLED sheet=… by=… batch=<n> count=<claims in the batch> total=<sum>`. The total adds up only the frozen dues of claims that ended up SETTLED, so PENDING claims and `n/a` dues are left out.

**Where the change is:**
- `claim/ClaimStatusChange.java`: added a `check(...)` method. It runs every refusal check of a status change and stops just before the first write. The single settle uses the same code path, so the two can't drift apart.
- `claim/BulkSettleClaims.java`: the check pass first, then the settle pass, then the `BATCH_SETTLED` line.
- `bulk-settle.POST.yml`: comment updated only. The front end didn't need any change, because it already shows the settled and refused counts the server returns.

**One known gap:** the checks run against the sheet as it is before any claim in the batch is settled. If settling one claim could change whether another selected claim passes (say, a per-person cap changing a due and so the proof-threshold check), the second pass could hit a refusal partway through. Earlier claims would then stay settled. The spec doesn't exercise this. Closing it fully would mean rolling back the database and holding back the audit lines when a refusal happens; I didn't do that because I couldn't confirm how the app's transaction handling would allow it.

probe.probe_text:
I changed nothing; this is all from reading the code. The main thing to know first: **the due arithmetic is written three times.** The screen works out every money figure itself in TypeScript. The server works out the same figures again in Java (`ClaimRepository`) for the audit, statements, period closes, settling and the permission thresholds. A third Java copy (`SheetAsOf`) handles statements taken "as of" a past date. --- ## 1. Figures and the rules behind them ### Claim row (`claims.slot.tsx`) | Figure (`data-testid`) | Rule | |---|---| | `claim-number` | Given when a DRAFT is **opened**, not when it is created. Sheet-wide 1, 2, 3… (`ClaimRepository.number`). With period numbering on (`numbersPerPeriod`: a period-numbering from-date is set and today is on or after it), it is `-`, or `X-` when the due-by is in no period (`numberInPeriod`). A rejected claim keeps its number, and so does a voided one (never reused). A split-off claim gets a new number. | | `claim-amount` | Two decimals. A negative amount is a **correction**: it must name, by number, a SETTLED claim of the same person, and only a negative amount may name one (`ClaimInput.checkCorrection`). | | `claim-date` | A blank date takes the sheet's **entry date**, or today when none is set, on add, paste and quick-add (`SheetRepository.entryDate`). On editing a draft, a blank date takes **today** instead (`SaveClaim`). That is an inconsistency. | | `claim-due-by` | Fixed when the claim is created (`ClaimRepository.dueBy`): the *terms*-th business day after the claim's date, skipping weekends and the sheet's holidays. Terms come from the person's own terms, else the grade's `terms-` in force on the date, else the sheet's `terms` (default 14). Editing a draft's date re-fixes it (`SaveClaim`). Adding a holiday re-fixes it for every claim that is not SETTLED or VOID and is due on or after that holiday (`refixDueBy`). Re-dating a claim does **not** change it. | | `claim-period` | The period containing the **due-by**, not the claim's date (`periodOf`). | | `claim-due` | `claimDueNow` (TS), which mirrors `ClaimRepository.dueNow`. Worked through in the next section. | | `claim-overdue` | `isOverdue`: the claim is OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and its **overdue-from** day is before today. Overdue-from = due-by + `grace-` days (calendar days), using the grade the person had on the claim's date and the grace in force then. | | `claim-stated` | The raw `stated` flag. Note that "bound" also needs the claim not to be PENDING (`Claim.bound`). | | `claim-deferred` / `-until` | Deferred = status OPEN and `deferredUntil` is after today. You can only defer an OPEN claim, to a date after today, and not in a closed period. A deferred claim counts in no total, is never overdue, cannot be settled or split, and a statement leaves it unbound. | | `claim-late-entry` | Set when the claim is added and its due-by falls in a **soft-closed** period (`lateEntry`). It also writes a `LATE_ENTRY` audit line. | | `claim-status` | DRAFT → OPEN → SETTLED. A clerk settling above the limit sends it to PENDING; a steward then approves (SETTLED) or rejects (back to OPEN). DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED claims can be voided. Rules are below. | | `claim-batch`, `claim-opened-by`, `claim-proofs`, `claim-reminded`, `claim-split-from`, `claim-log`, `claim-comments` | Stored values. Reminding is allowed once per "today", for OPEN or PENDING claims only. A proof can be added unless the claim is SETTLED or VOID, or in a closed period. Each log line records the due as computed on the server at that moment. | ### How a claim's due is worked out (`dueNow` / `claimDueNow`) 1. **Settled:** the due frozen at settlement (`settled_due`) is shown as is. 2. **Otherwise the claim needs a figure** (`figure`): - A bound statement figure is used, or `n/a` when the statement bound it to n/a. - Else the **live rate figure** (`due`): amount × rate ÷ 100. - Rate = the rate of the grade the person had **on the claim's date**, using the rate with the latest from-date on or before that date. An undated rate applies from the beginning of time. - There is no figure (`n/a`) when that rate's to-date is before the claim's date. 3. **Rounding** (`rounding` / `roundsHalfUp`): - Half up when the claim is dated before the sheet's **policy date** (a blank policy date means today). Otherwise half to even. - A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects. 4. **Late charge** (`lateCharge` / `withCharge`), only while overdue: - For every full 30 days past overdue-from, apply the `late-pct` in force on that 30-day boundary. - Each charge is taken on figure + earlier charges (it **compounds**) and is rounded on its own. - A statement never binds the charge; it keeps growing with today until settlement freezes it. 5. **Floor:** the result is at least the `floor` in force on the claim's date (default 1.00). 6. **Corrections** (negative amounts) get no floor and no late charge. ### Which claims count (`Claim.counts` / `counts`) - A claim counts if it is **SETTLED**, or if it is **OPEN/PENDING**, not deferred, and either bound by a statement or not dated inside one of the person's **holds**. - **Retirement:** once today is on or after the retirement date, the person is treated as held over every date (`liveHolds` / `holdsById`). Their unbound open claims then drop out of all live totals. - **For periods** (`countsAs` / `countsOn`): a claim counts by the status its log shows at the end of the period's last day. Holds only remove claims that are still open now. ### Person row | Figure | Rule | |---|---| | `person-claimed` | Sum of the **amounts** of counting claims. The TS version adds them with floating-point `Number` math; everything else uses exact cents. | | `person-due-total` | Sum of `dueNow` over counting claims, skipping `n/a`, held to the **cap** in force on today. It shows `n/a` only when no rate for the person's grade is in force today **and** no counting claim has a fixed figure or a due. | | `person-excess` | How far the uncapped sum is above the cap, else 0.00. | | `person-settled-total` / `-open-total` | The uncapped due-total split by SETTLED vs OPEN/PENDING. | | `person-overdue-count` / `-total` | Counting claims that are overdue, and the sum of their dues. | | `person-aged-0-30/31-60/61` | Dues of counting OPEN/PENDING claims, bucketed by days since the claim's date (frontend only). | | `person-active` | Has a counting open claim dated within the last 30 days, today included (frontend only). | | `person-period-

-due-total` | Open period: dues of counting claims whose **due-by** falls in the period. Closed or soft-closed: the per-person total frozen at close (0.00 for anyone added since). | | `person-statement-count`, `-stated-total`, `-statement-date` | Set by taking a statement (below). | | `person-backing` | Frozen dues of the person's patrons' SETTLED claims dated in the last 90 days. | | `person-grade` | The grade in force on today: the one with the latest from-date on or before it. The first grade applies from the beginning of time. A save that leaves the grade unchanged with a blank from-date records no new grade. | ### Sheet-level figures - **`rollup-due-total`, `header-due-total`, `rollup-overdue-total`, `header-overdue-total`** use `trimmedSum`: people's figures added up, leaving out the single highest and lowest when three or more people have one. The server's `Rollup.trimmed` does the same for the audit. - **`rollup-claimed-total`, `rollup-settled-total`, `rollup-open-total`, `rollup-overdue-count`** are plain sums. - **`summary-grade--due-total`** is a plain sum of the capped person totals, with retired people left out. **`-count`** and **`-active`** count people the same way. - **Period figures:** - `period-due-total` and `summary-period-*` are the sum of the per-person period totals. - `period-closed` shows yes, soft or no. - **Other totals:** - `month-*-due-total` groups counting dues by the claim's **date** month. - `tag-*-due-total` groups them by tag; a claim with two tags counts in both. - `header-claims-*-count` and `summary-status-*` count claims by status. - `summary-void-*` counts VOID claims by void reason. - **Rates:** - `rate-current-` is the grade's rate in force today, or `n/a`. - `rate-preview-count` and `-diff` are frontend only. They re-run `claimDueNow` with a candidate rate over open claims of that grade (the grade on the claim's date). ### What gets frozen, and when - **Settle or approve** freezes `dueNow` at that moment into `settled_due`: the bound figure if it has one, late charge and floor included. A PENDING claim's figure is live. A claim with no figure settles as `n/a` and stays live. **Re-settle** (steward only, not in a closed period) re-freezes the claim as if it were OPEN and unbound today. - **Statement** (`TakeStatement`): - Records the person's due-total, capped. - Binds each counting claim to its figure *without* the floor or late charge, or to `n/a` when the rate has ended. - Unbinds every non-counting claim. - A PENDING claim gets `stated` set but isn't "bound" until it leaves PENDING. - **As of a date:** the date must be on or before today and the person must have existed then. The binding is replayed from history (`SheetAsOf`). - **Cancel** is steward only. It unbinds all the person's claims, and the earlier statement's bindings are *not* restored. - **Close / soft-close a period** (`PeriodCloser`) freezes the period total and every person's total for it. - **Close:** every change to a claim whose due-by falls in the period is refused (`PeriodGuard`). That covers add, edit/lock, open, settle, void, defer, split, proof, redate, reassign, resettle and paste. - **Soft-close:** the figures are frozen but changes are still allowed. New claims added into it are marked late entries. - **Reopen** drops the frozen figures. - **Auto-close:** when today changes, each open period whose to-date + `graceDays` is before today closes (`auto=yes`). - **Changing today** writes one SNAPSHOT line per person, releases all editor locks, auto-closes lapsed periods and writes ROLLUP/TOTALS lines. ### Who may do what - **Roles:** clerk (the default), steward, viewer. Someone acts as a steward while a delegation covers today (`role`). - **Viewers, as-of screens, archived sheets:** `RefuseViewer` guards every endpoint that changes the sheet, except the bulk ones. A viewer changes nothing, an as-of screen changes nothing, and an archived sheet refuses everything. - **Permission matrix** (`allows`) covers open, settle, void and close (clerk and steward by default) and reassign and reopen (steward only by default). - **Settle and approve** (`ClaimStatusChange`): - Whoever opened a claim cannot settle or approve it. - Whoever last edited it cannot settle or approve it either. - A deferred claim cannot be settled. - Above the **proof threshold** (the grade's in force on the claim's date, else the sheet's), a claim needs at least one proof. - A clerk settling above the **clerk limit** sends the claim to PENDING instead. - Only stewards approve or reject; a reject needs a reason. - **Opening:** a claim with an empty note cannot be opened when its due is above the **note threshold**. - **Voiding:** - While the sheet has void reasons, a void needs one of them. - Voiding a SETTLED claim is steward only, and only within 7 days of the settle date in its log. - **Steward only:** redate, resettle, cancel a statement, archive the sheet, delegate (by their own role only, and not to themselves). - **Editing:** only a DRAFT can be edited, under a per-user lock. - **Retirement:** no claim may be dated after the retirement date (`claimAllowed`). - **Bulk actions:** - Bulk-settle is all-or-nothing. - Bulk-open and bulk-reassign go claim by claim and count refusals. - Bulk-grade does nothing when the user is a viewer. ### Imports - **Paste:** each line is `name,amount,date,note[ #ref]`. Every line is checked first and one bad line refuses the whole paste. People are matched by name, ignoring case. Claims are added as drafts. - **Quick-add:** adds a draft dated on the entry date, creating the person with grade A when the name is new. ### Inconsistencies I noticed in passing - **Anyone not a viewer can set roles**, including making themselves a steward: `SaveRole` has no steward check. The same goes for settings, rates, holidays, holds, retirement and statements. - **Stale comments:** - `statusCounts.ts` says no claim is ever PENDING. - `useClaims.ts` says a voided claim loses its number; the server keeps it. - The `Settings` type says a due-by landing on a holiday moves to the next day; the server counts business days. ## 2. How hard this was to find and follow The logic is scattered and tangled, not in one place a new developer could pick up. The due, counting, rounding and late-charge rules are written three times: `ClaimRepository`/`Rollup` in Java, `useOverdue.ts`/`useRates.ts`/`useDueTotals.ts` in TypeScript, and `SheetAsOf` in Java. Each total is re-assembled separately in about ten frontend hooks. The permission and freezing rules are spread over dozens of small action classes, the YAML guard steps and long doc comments, which are sometimes out of date. You can only see the whole picture by reading roughly 30 files side by side.
